title: Scheduler Injection and Fidelity Rollback Lab Manual
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview

Purpose
- This document defines a reproducible lab procedure for injecting scheduler-level perturbations against the serving runtime, observing fidelity regressions, and executing an automated rollback of fidelity-reducing changes. The intent is to provide a safe, auditable experiment protocol that engineering and SRE teams can run in the staging and canary environments.

Scope
- Applies to runtime scheduler, kernel admission controller, and the fidelity orchestration layer.
- Environments: staging (required), canary (recommended), production (only for validated runbooks and with approval).

When to use this runbook
1. Before rolling out a new scheduler policy or kernel variant that affects priority, preemption, or coalescing.
2. When reproducing a customer-facing fidelity regression trace.
3. To benchmark rollback and fallthrough guarantees under controlled degradation.

Background and rationale
- Recent work on predictive slotting and admission controllers introduced priority-reshaping heuristics. These heuristics can inadvertently change effective model fidelity under bursty traffic (e.g., quantization swap or kernel variant downgrade). The lab manual captures a safe method to simulate scheduler mis-behaviour, measure fidelity impact using our eval harness, and validate rollback safety.

High-level testbed architecture (text diagram)
- Components:
  - Traffic generator (tg-load) -> Request router -> Scheduler/Admission controller -> Kernel variants on GPU nodes -> Observability collectors (trace/metrics) -> Eval harness and fidelity oracle
- Text diagram: [tg-load] -> [router] -> [scheduler-admission] -> [gpu-kernel-pool: vA/vB] -> [observability: otel, runtime-metrics, fidelity-evals]

Prerequisites (environment and access)
| Item | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Staging cluster | yes | kube context: staging-runtime-admin |
| Canary namespace | recommended | canary runtime-namespace: redwood-canary |
| Experiment CRD installed | yes | chart: runtime-chaos/1.3.0 |
| Telemetry hooks enabled | yes | traces + metrics (otel + prometheus) |
| Eval harness snapshot | yes | prompt-set: fidelity-smoke-v3 |
| Owner on-call | yes | listed in ownership section below |

Safety rules and approvals
- Never run injection on production without written approval from Eng SRE and Product Security.
- Maintain an experiment ticket in the Experiment Registry with start/end times and rollback criteria.
- Quotas: inject only up to 20% of scheduler decision streams during a single test.

Success criteria and SLOs to watch (staging/canary baseline)
- Latency SLO baseline: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 300ms for generator workload.
- Error rate: application-level 5xx < 0.1% above baseline.
- Fidelity: pass rate on fidelity-smoke-v3 >= baseline - 2 percentage points. If regression > 2pp, trigger rollback.
- GPU utilization: sustained increase > 30% above baseline for > 3 minutes -> investigate kernel thrash.

Experiment types supported
1. Priority inversion injection: re-label incoming requests with low priority after scheduler decision to simulate admission misclassification.
2. Kernel downgrade bloom: force a subset of requests to be routed to a lower-fidelity kernel variant (vB) for an interval.
3. Prefetch delay: add artificial delay in kvcache prefetch path to emulate missing warmups.
4. Admission flood: increase admission GC frequency to create eviction churn.

Safe experiment template (YAML)
- Example CRD (apply to staging only):
  apiVersion: chaos.redwood.ai/v1
  kind: SchedulerInjection
  metadata:
    name: fidelity-downgrade-smoke-1
    namespace: staging-experiments
  spec:
    type: kernel-downgrade
    targetPercentage: 10
    duration: 10m
    injectionWindow: 09:00-09:20Z
    rollbackCondition:
      fidelityDropPct: 2.0
      p95IncreaseMs: 50

Step-by-step procedure
1. Create experiment ticket in Experiment Registry and notify on-call. Include start/stop window and rollback policy.
2. Verify telemetry: run quick smoke to collect baseline metrics (run for 5 minutes). Command: kubectl --context staging-runtime-admin run tg-load --image=redwood/tg-load:stable -- ... (see quickstart args in the experiment repo).
3. Deploy experiment CRD to staging: kubectl apply -f scheduler-injection-smoke.yaml -n staging-experiments.
4. Monitor the observability dashboard (link below) and the fidelity runner.
5. If fidelity regression exceeds rollbackCondition, execute rollback (automated by the experiment controller) or manual rollback: kubectl delete schedulerinjection fidelity-downgrade-smoke-1 -n staging-experiments.
6. Run post-experiment eval: curl -X POST https://staging-evals.internal/api/run -d '{"suite":"fidelity-smoke-v3"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_TOKEN'

Observability checklist (metrics and traces)
- Metrics (Prometheus names):
  - runtime_request_latency_seconds{quantile="0.95"}
  - runtime_request_errors_total{code=~"5.."}
  - scheduler_decision_latency_seconds
  - kernel_variant_served_total{variant="vA|vB"}
  - gpu_kernel_thrash_events_total
- Traces: correlate a sample of slow requests with scheduler.trace_id and kernel.variant tag.
- Logs: watch for admission-controller WARN entries: "eviction-loop" and "kernel-fallback".

Automated rollback detection rules (experiment controller)
- Primary triggers (immediate rollback):
  - fidelityDropPct >= 2.0 for the eval suite window.
  - p95 latency increase >= configured p95IncreaseMs (default 50ms).
  - sustained 5xx delta >= 0.2% over 60s.
- Secondary triggers (escalation):
  - GPU utilization > 95% for > 2 minutes.
  - Kernel handshake failures > 5/min.

Manual mitigation playbook (if automation fails)
1. Pause ingress to the canary namespace: kubectl scale deployment/router --replicas=0 -n redwood-canary
2. Force route to baseline kernel variant: curl -X POST https://runtime-admin.staging.internal/routing/set -d '{"force_variant":"vA"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
3. Rebalance kvcache shards: runtime-opctl rebalance --scope=canary --shards=8
4. If nodes are unstable, cordon and drain affected GPU nodes: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

Post-experiment analysis and artifacts
- Required artifacts to attach to the experiment ticket:
  - baseline and during-run Prometheus snapshots (5m each).
  - 50 representative traces (trace-ids or zipped spans).
  - Eval harness results (JSON), including per-prompt failure reasons.
  - Kernel variant counters and admission-decision logs.
- Template for postmortem summary (1 paragraph plus bullets):
  - What we changed (experiment spec)
  - What we observed (metrics & fidelity delta)
  - Root cause hypothesis
  - Remediation / follow-ups (owners and due dates)

Appendix A — Example quick commands
- Baseline snapshot: kubectl run tg-load --image=redwood/tg-load:stable --command -- /bin/sh -c 'tg-run --profile=small-burst --duration=300' --context=staging-runtime-admin
- Trigger manual downgrade via admin API:
  curl -X POST https://runtime-admin.staging.internal/experiments/manual-downgrade -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -d '{"percent":10, "variant":"vB", "reason":"test"}'

Appendix B — Common failure modes and troubleshooting notes
- Symptom: fidelity drop without latency increase. Likely root cause: routing mislabeling or eval harness mismatch. Check kernel_variant_served_total and request-tag propagation.
- Symptom: p95 spikes but fidelity stable. Likely cause: kernel thrash or prefetch delays. Check gpu_kernel_thrash_events_total and kvcache-miss rates.
- Symptom: automation fails to rollback. Check experiment controller logs (controller-manager) and the event stream: kubectl -n staging-experiments get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
